These policies include occurrence-based and claims-made insurance.   1. **Occurrence-based policy**: Provides coverage as long as the loss occurred while the policy was active, accommodating situations that may not result in immediate claims or lawsuits. The aggregate limit resets every year, offering renewed coverage [Source 1], [Source 5].  2. **Claims-made policy**: Coverage only takes effect when a claim is filed during the policy period. Once a claim is paid that reaches the aggregate limit, there will be no further protection. The coverage purchased must last for the duration of the policy [Source 1], [Source 5].

Some of the services provided by these clinics include:  1. **One-stop clinics**: These clinics offer multiple services simultaneously or in sequence during a single visit. Patients can receive all aspects of their outpatient care in one visit, minimizing disruption to work or other commitments and reducing the stress and cost of multiple hospital visits [Source 1].  2. **Drop-in clinics**: These clinics provide specified times when clinicians are available for patients undergoing or recently receiving treatment to speak to the care team. They can serve as points of contact for concerns or questions, sometimes replacing follow-up clinics when there is no clinical requirement to see patients [Source 4].  These clinics aim to efficiently use resources, focus care on patients in need, and provide a better-attended and improved service for patients by understanding their needs and delivering comprehensive care [Source 1], [Source 2], [Source 3].
